title: How To Handle A Bully Colleague
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Prompted by his own recent encounter with a colleague's subtle bullying, Linsin shares six lessons for handling a bullying coworker. The approach centers on quiet, unyielding resistance rather than retaliation: taking the high road instead of fighting fire with fire, holding persistent eye contact because bullies are uncomfortable being looked at directly, and calmly refusing demands with a flat 'No, I'm not going to do that.' Consistency is key — repeated calm resistance over time wears bullies down since they seek out people who won't push back. When the bully eventually approaches with a sheepish apology or unsolicited advice, Linsin recommends accepting the apology but firmly stating you don't want their advice again, framing this as a kindness that helps them save face while ending the pattern for good.
points: Take the high road rather than fighting fire with fire, since retaliation guarantees an endless battle and matches the bully's level.
Hold persistent, direct eye contact during snide remarks — bullies are cowards who can't tolerate being looked at steadily.
Resist politely and calmly rather than ignoring provocations, since avoidance only empowers a bully further.
Respond to pushback with a flat, unmovable refusal such as 'No, I'm not going to do that,' without arguing or backing down.
Sustain the resistance consistently over time; bullies target easy, timid prey and will eventually back off from someone who never wavers.
quotes: But in the long run you’ll be so glad you took it. Not only for your own peace of mind and self-worth, but because it weakens the bully and their power over you.
Bullies are cowards, and they can’t stand eye contact. By just looking them in the eye—and holding it—whenever they make a snide remark, you make them uncomfortable.
To resist, I’ve found that just saying “No, I’m not going to do that”—and then holding your ground with direct eye contact—is the most powerful response.
Don’t go back on your word. Don’t argue your point. Just stick to your guns, unmovable, like an iron stake hammered into frozen ground.
But if you’re consistent and don’t give in, they’ll back down. They’ll stop speaking to you or even looking in your direction.
Calmly say, “I don’t want to hear advice from you again” or “never again tell me what to do.
